To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) palladium contacts to semiconducting carbon nanotubes can be used to make ballistic nanotube transistors with current carrying capability approaching 25uA; (2) in situ hydrogen treatment of palladium contacts can be used to control the Schottky barrier height and to tune the device characteristics; and (3) the current saturation in these devices is limited by optical phonon scattering.
palladium contacts to single wall nanotubes eliminate Schottky barriers and enable ballistic transport in semiconducting tubes.

palladium contacts to semiconducting carbon nanotubes can eliminate or greatly reduce the energy barriers for transport through these tubes, and thus enable the realization of ballistic nanotube transistors with high performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the physics and chemistry at the metal carbon nanotube interfaces, which are crucial for nanotube device applications.
understanding the electronic transport properties of single wall carbon nanotubes and the effect of the contacts on the transport properties.
the development of new nanoscale electronic and photonic devices based on the unique properties of nanotubes and nanowires.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated the first ballistic field effect transistores with zero or slightly positive Schottky barriers.
the Pd contacts to the semiconducting tubes provide the best contacts yet reported, and that the contacts to the metallic tubes are also improved, although not to the same degree.
the Pd contacts provide a low barrier, and that this low barrier allows the device to behave like a ballistic conductor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that it is possible to fabricate ballistic carbon nanotube transistors.
we have shown how to fabricate high performance nanotube field transistors by using a metal with high work functions.
the Pd contacts to semiconducting tubes can be made to be either Ohmic (metallic) or Schottky (semiconducting) depending on the Fermi level of the metal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

by using noble metals with high work functions, the Schottky barriers at the nanotubes metal junctions can be greatly reduced or eliminated, and the 'ON' conductance of nanotube transistors can approach the ballistic limit.
the Schottky barrier can be eliminated or reduced by proper choice of the electrode material.
the performance of nanotube field-effect transistors can be dramatically improved by using high work function metals with good wetting interactions for contacts.
